historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari, Ibn Jamhur, Al-Fihrist, Volume 1, Page 150. Musabi ibn Umair Al-Khuza'i was a prominent scholar and poet of the early Islamic period who lived from 581-642 AH (1186-1244 AD). He was a well-known historian and a member of the Khuza'a tribe. Musabi was a student of the famous scholar Ibn Mujahid and was also the teacher of Ibn Qutaybah, another prominent scholar. He is known for his works on Arabic grammar, poetry, and history.

Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, Chapter 2, Section 1. Musabi ibn Umair Al-Khuza'i is mentioned in Ibn Khaldun's seminal work as a prominent scholar and historian of the early Islamic period. He is described as a learned man who was well-versed in various sciences, including history and grammar. Musabi's works were known for their accuracy and detail, and he is considered an important source for early Islamic history.
